name: Akiflow
tagline: Unified task inbox and time-blocking planner with 30+ app integrations
painPoints: No free plan — only a 7-day trial before a paid plan kicks in
Time-blocking requires manual drag-and-drop scheduling each day
Consolidates tasks from other apps but does not create tasks automatically from email
AI features are limited to writing assistance rather than proactive management
Desktop-heavy; mobile experience is less capable
metaDescription: Looking for an Akiflow alternative? GAIA is source-available AI that triages email, manages tasks, and runs workflows across your tools. Free tier included.
whyPeopleLook: Akiflow appeals to power users who want to aggregate all their tasks from Asana, Jira, Todoist, and Gmail into one inbox and then time-block their day. The command bar and keyboard shortcuts make it fast, and the calendar integration is tight. But even with 30+ integrations, Akiflow still requires you to review the inbox and manually schedule tasks into time blocks every day. It does not read email to create tasks automatically, has no AI reasoning that adjusts to changing priorities, and offers no free tier to try before committing.
gaiaReplaces: Unified task inbox aggregating tasks from multiple tools
Email-to-task creation without manual task entry or inbox review
Calendar-aware task prioritization that suggests scheduling automatically
Daily work planning via AI briefings instead of manual time-blocking
Cross-tool workflow automation beyond task aggregation
gaiaAdvantages: Tasks created automatically from email: no manual inbox review required
Proactive scheduling suggestions based on calendar availability
Free tier available; Akiflow has no free plan
Source-available and self-hostable for complete data control
MCP integrations alongside native email and calendar management
migrationSteps: Export tasks from Akiflow or connected tools
Connect GAIA to Gmail so it auto-creates tasks from email
Link Google Calendar for scheduling intelligence
Set up GAIA's daily briefing to replace Akiflow's manual time-blocking review

faqs.question: Does GAIA have a command bar like Akiflow?
faqs.answer: GAIA uses a conversational interface rather than a keyboard-driven command bar. You can create and manage tasks through natural language, which is faster than switching to a dedicated command palette.

faqs.question: Can GAIA time-block tasks into my calendar like Akiflow?
faqs.answer: GAIA provides calendar-aware scheduling suggestions and can create calendar events for tasks. It focuses more on proactive prioritization than hard time-block enforcement, which gives you flexibility when plans change.

faqs.question: Is GAIA cheaper than Akiflow?
faqs.answer: Akiflow is a paid plan with no free tier. GAIA Pro is ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month with a free tier and self-hosting option. Self-hosted GAIA is free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs), making it significantly more accessible.

faqs.question: Does GAIA aggregate tasks from tools like Asana and Jira like Akiflow?
faqs.answer: GAIA can connect to multiple task sources via MCP integrations, including reading tasks from connected tools and creating a unified view. Its primary advantage over Akiflow is the AI layer that creates and prioritizes tasks automatically.

comparisonRows.gaia: Assistant that plans the day from email and calendar instead of showing tasks to drag into time blocks
comparisonRows.competitor: Unified task inbox and calendar time-blocker: aggregates tasks from 30+ tools into one prioritized view and lets you time-block them with drag-and-drop

comparisonRows.gaia: Creates tasks itself from Gmail and meeting outcomes, so there is nothing to aggregate by hand
comparisonRows.competitor: Aggregates existing tasks from connected tools (Asana, Jira, Todoist, Linear, etc.); creates new tasks via natural language or keyboard shortcuts; does not create tasks from email content autonomously

comparisonRows.gaia: Full inbox management: triages Gmail, drafts replies, and converts emails into scheduled tasks
comparisonRows.competitor: Gmail integration as a task source: email items can be added to Akiflow's inbox; no triage, reply drafting, or autonomous email management

comparisonRows.gaia: Schedules tasks against real calendar availability and reshuffles when meetings move, with no drag-and-drop session
comparisonRows.competitor: Core strength: drag tasks into calendar time slots; syncs Google Calendar and Outlook; shows meetings alongside tasks for unified daily planning

comparisonRows.gaia: One AI-assembled briefing across Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion, and the rest of your tools, replacing the morning review ritual
comparisonRows.competitor: Core strength: aggregates tasks from 30+ tools (Asana, Jira, Linear, Notion, GitHub, Todoist, Slack) into one prioritized inbox with full keyboard control

comparisonRows.gaia: AI that executes across tools, not just parses dates: it drafts, schedules, and follows up on your behalf
comparisonRows.competitor: Natural language task creation (date parsing, recurrence); limited AI; the intelligence is in the aggregation UX and keyboard workflow, not AI automation

comparisonRows.gaia: Natural-language automations spanning email, calendar, and tasks, with no per-workflow setup in connected tools
comparisonRows.competitor: No native automation engine; relies on connected tools for task creation; Zapier integration for additional workflows

comparisonRows.gaia: Surfaces conflicts, deadlines, and follow-ups continuously, so planning never waits for a manual session
comparisonRows.competitor: Reactive: aggregates and displays tasks that exist elsewhere; requires manual planning session to organize and time-block

comparisonRows.competitor: Closed-source SaaS; no self-hosting; no free plan: 7-day trial only
